intro:
You're a business owner whose home address is one search away? It probably is. People-search sites list your address, your cell and your family, and if you own a business, your LLC filing can tie your home to the company while lead-list sites scrape your direct line and your team's emails.

I asked ChatGPT to find all of it and help me take it down. This is the exact setup: the search prompt, the sites to check first, the agent-mode prompt that works through the opt-out forms, and the weekly check that keeps you off.

free.title: Step 1: Gather what they'd search for (5 minutes)
free.body:
Write down every version of you that might be listed. The AI can only find what you tell it to look for.

  • Full name, plus nicknames and maiden or former names
  • Current home address and the last two or three you've had
  • Personal cell, plus any old numbers
  • Personal and business email addresses
  • Business name, LLC name and registered agent address
  • City, state and your approximate age (these sites group people by age)

Before you start: opting out is free on most sites. Never pay a site to remove you. Use a separate email address for the opt-out confirmations, and don't send a photo of your ID to a site that only asks for it "to verify". Look for another way first.

free.title: Step 2: The search prompt
free.body:
Paste this into ChatGPT or Claude with web search turned on.

Copy this inSearch the web for everything publicly listed about me. Name: [full name, other names] City/state: [city, state] Age: [approx] Business: [business / LLC name] Find every people-search site, data broker and lead-list site that is selling, listing or sharing my personal or business information. Make a table with: site name | what it shows (address, phone, relatives, email, employer) | the official opt-out or removal page link | what the opt-out needs (email, form, phone call, ID). Then give me a recommended removal order, biggest sites first. Only include links to the sites' own official opt-out pages.

Check every link it gives you before you use it. AI can get web addresses wrong, so make sure each one is on the site's own domain.

free.title: Step 3: The sites to check first
free.body:
Most removal lists start with these. Each one runs its own opt-out.

  • People-search sites: Whitepages, Spokeo, TruePeopleSearch, FastPeopleSearch, BeenVerified, PeopleConnect (the Intelius family), Radaris
  • B2B lead lists: ZoomInfo, Apollo, RocketReach, SignalHire

The lead-list sites matter most for business owners. That's where your direct line and your team's emails end up in other people's cold-outreach tools.

free.title: Step 4: Let agent mode do the forms
free.body:
In ChatGPT, turn on agent mode and give it the table from Step 2.

Copy this inGo through this removal list one site at a time. For each site, open the official opt-out page, find my listing, and fill in the removal request using only the details I give you here: [name, city, the email for confirmations]. Stop and ask me before you submit anything that asks for payment, an ID upload, or a phone verification code. Keep a log: site, date, status, anything I still need to do.

Stay nearby. Some sites send a confirmation email or show a CAPTCHA, and you'll need to do those yourself.

free.title: Step 5: Make it weekly
free.body:
Listings come back, because data brokers keep re-scraping public records. Schedule this to run every week.

Copy this inEvery week: re-run my search from the removal log. Tell me which sites still show my information, which removals are confirmed, and anything new. Then request removal again wherever my listing reappeared.

free.title: Step 6: Close the business leaks
free.body:
• Put a registered agent or virtual office address on your LLC filing instead of your home address, where your state allows it.
  • Have your team opt out of ZoomInfo, Apollo and RocketReach for their work emails, or do it for them.
  • Use a business line on your website and listings instead of your personal cell.
  • Make sure your domain's WHOIS privacy is turned on.

Keep a simple removal log: site, date requested, confirmed or not, and when to check again.

Not legal advice. Opt-out rules differ by site and by state, and some states give you extra deletion rights. Check yours.
